newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish bonds firm in subdued trade.
newsitem.headline: Irish bonds firm in subdued trade.

text.p: Irish government bonds made some gains in sombre trade on Monday as the market awaited fresh factors to stimulate activity further, dealers said.

"Dublin is moving parallel with European markets but the U.S. holiday is obviously putting a damper on activity," one dealer said, adding that Wednesday's U.S. FOMC meeting was also keeping a lid on trade," he added.
By 1613 GMT the eight percent bond due 2000 was 12p stronger at 106.18 to yield 6.09 percent while the eight percent bond due 2006 was 20p stronger at 107.80 to yield 6.75 percent.
The eight percent bond due 2015 was 110.90, a rise of 20p.
"Currency markets will again remain a side-show this week, and the U.S. dollar's activity will have to be watched as well as the sterling/punt situation at home," one dealer said.
Dealers said the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting on Wednesday would probably not yield any change in interest rates.
"The FOMC meeting and the ECOFIN meeting in Dublin will be closely monitored for any comments or developments," one dealer said.
Dealers said the bulk of the week's data would be released in the UK and the U.S.
